【環境】 Coal power lives longer next to data centres
item.description: Data centres are among the world’s fastest growing electricity consumers. An analysis of more than 9,000 facilities worldwide links the artificial intelligence-era expansion of data centres to delayed coal plant retirements and around 2 Gt of additional carbon dioxide emissions.

item.title: 【環境】 Higher warming leads to a larger zero-emissions commitment
item.description: Scientific grounds for a net-zero policy assume near-zero committed warming over a few decades after CO2 emissions cease. A modelling study suggests that if prior peak temperatures rise above 2 °C before cessation of CO2 emissions, committed warming increases, making it harder to stabilize global warming.

item.title: 【環境】 Early evidence links data centre exposure to coal power retirement timelines
item.description: Data centre expansion may slow the coal-fired power plants phase-out, complicating decarbonization pathways. This study finds that coal units exposed to post-2020 data centres have lower retirement risks and their potential lifetime extensions could cause large additional CO2 emissions.

item.title: 【環境】 Widespread North American pollution and health impacts from early twentieth century copper production
item.description: Mining and industrial emissions can be substantially reduced by technological interventions. The historical case of copper production in Anaconda, Montana shows the widespread health burdens that can result when lax regulation delays such interventions.

item.title: 【環境】 Agricultural data source choice as a dominant control on nitrogen surplus uncertainty
item.description: Environmental impacts from nitrogen surplus in agricultural regions make it critical to understand the nature and drivers of excess nitrogen. Bhaduri and colleagues show that data source uncertainty must be accounted for to avoid misalignments in management and mitigation decisions.

item.title: 【AI4S】 Filter By:
item.description: Safe and effective gene delivery remains a central challenge for therapeutic applications. While non-viral and viral vectors have enabled substantial progress, their reliance on non-human components often triggers immune responses, limiting their use in chronic treatments. Here, we develop DeepDelivery, an artificial intelligence-driven platform to identify human proteins with scaffold potential for mRNA delivery. Proteome-scale screening nominated 512 candidates, and experimental validation show that 12 of 15 selected human proteins functioned as scaffold components that facilitated particle formation and mRNA delivery within a modular engineering framework. Notably, several tripartite motif (TRIM) family proteins, typically linked to antiviral responses, exhibit strong assembly and delivery activity. Model interpretability and perturbation analyses identify TRIM domain features that influenced prediction scores and guide TRIM25-specific domain engineering to improve delivery. Together, these results establish a framework for mining the human proteome for scaffold components of programmable mRNA delivery systems and for further exploring the design space of human-derived delivery
